chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Frankie Newton sessions of 1937 and 1939: personnel

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The records that you made with him were kind of the forerunner of the John Kirby band.

They were all, because a lot of the guys on there.... Not a lot of them but the later, the first edition of that band had Don Frye as the piano player. Let's see who else was on there. There was Frankie, and I guess he did the arrangements, right?

And Edmund Hall, Pete Brown and Cecil Scott, Don Frye, John Smith on guitar, Dick Fulbright--we talked about him earlier--you and Clarence Palmer the vocalist. And those were the ones for March 5th, 1937, and you did some ones on April 15th, a month later with Russell Procope and Slim Gaillard. Otherwise it was the same band. In 1939 it was Frankie, Mezz Mezzrow ... Pete Brown, James P.
Johnson, Al Casey, John Kirby and you. Do you remember those sessions at all?
Yeah, yeah, but I'm trying to remember as you were reading them down, you know.
I'll read you the titles. "You're the One," "You Showed Me the Way."
(Singing) "You Showed me the Way." And this Clarence Palmer was singing on quite a few of those.
Right. "Please Don't Talk About Me When I'm Gone."
